newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to summon leading politicians over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to summon leading politicians over scandal.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors will summon for questioning on Friday three senior politicians named by the founder of the stricken Hanbo Group as taking his money, a prosecution official said on Thursday.
Kim Deog-ryong, a leading ruling party lawmaker and member of President Kim Young-sam's inner circle, is among the three, he said.

The other two are Kim Sang-hyun, a senior lawmaker with the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, and Kim Yong-hwan, secretary-general of the United Liberal Democrats, a smaller opposition party, the official said.
The three are among 33 people Chung Tae-soo said he had given money to as "political funds", the official said. Prosecutors plan to question the other 30 later, he added, declining to name them.
Of the total, 20 are members of parliament -- 13 from the ruling New Korea Party, four from National Congress and two from the United Liberal Democrats and one from the Democratic Party.
"We have decided to summon all people in the Chung Tae-soo list to clear up public doubts," the official said.
